question.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to ${\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r,$ where $F(x,y)=(x+y)^{2}\,i+{e}^{x-y}\,j$ and $C$ is the line segment traversed from the point $A(-2,1)$ to the point $B(1,-1)?$

*Hint: Use the parametrization $r(t)=(-2+3t)\,i+(1-2t)\,j.$*
question.worked_solution:
We will use the formula

$$
{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r={\int }_{a}^{b}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we need to parameterize the line segment.
The position vectors of the endpoints of our line segment are 
$a=-2\,i+j$ and $b=i-j.$
So, the parametrization of the line segment is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =a+t(b-a) \\  & =(-2\,i+j)+t[(i-j)-(-2\,i+j)] \\  & =(-2\,i+j)+t(3\,i-2\,j) \\  & =(-2+3t)\,i+(1-2t)\,j,\end{aligned}
$$

where $t$ varies from $t=0$ (at the point $A$) to $t=1$ (at the point $B$).
Thus, along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=-2+3t,\,y=1-2t.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(x+y)^{2}\,i+{e}^{x-y}\,j \\  & =(-2+3t+1-2t)^{2}\,i+{e}^{-2+3t-(1-2t)}\,j \\  & =(t-1)^{2}\,i+{e}^{5t-3}\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing ${r}^{′}(t),$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2+3t)i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1-2t)j \\  & =3\,i-2\,j.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) & =((t-1)^{2}\,i+{e}^{5t-2}\,j)\cdot (3\,i-2\,j) \\  & =(t-1)^{2}\cdot 3+{e}^{5t-3}\cdot (-2) \\  & =3(t-1)^{2}-2{e}^{5t-3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we can write the integral as 

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{C}F\cdot \text{d}r & ={\int }_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}3(t-1)^{2}-2{e}^{5t-3}\,dt.\end{aligned}
$$
